pages.organisations.whatBody.source: Four courses for learners aged about 10 to 17. Exploring Our World: {ourWorld} lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life. Digital World: {digitalWorld} lessons about AI and the digital world. Southeast Asia Through Time: {southeastAsia} lessons about the region's past, from real objects, maps and letters. Art, Architecture and Society: {art} lessons about works and buildings from around the world. Most lessons have five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect (four where a lesson has no video, as every lesson does in Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu and Tiếng Việt). It runs in a web browser on shared laptops and tablets, in English, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu or Tiếng Việt. Lessons work offline once a course is saved on the device; the optional videos need the internet.

pages.about.missionBody.source: Thinkerwell began with a love of social studies and a question: how can more youth have the chance to explore the world they live in? We built a free digital platform to make digital learning tools and social studies education accessible to youth facing barriers to education. Our goal is to help learners ask questions, grow their critical thinking skills, explore diverse perspectives, and share their own ideas.

pages.about.missionBody.back: Thinkerwell began from a love of social science and a question: how can more young people have the chance to explore the world they live in? Our goal is to help learners ask questions, develop critical thinking skills, explore diverse perspectives and share their own ideas.

siteVideo.explore.p1.source: Every learner deserves the chance to explore the world they live in. But across Southeast Asia, many youth face barriers to education. In Myanmar, about 3.8 million people are displaced inside their own country. In Malaysia, refugee children can't attend government schools. And in East Asia and the Pacific, one in three school-age children had no internet at home.
siteVideo.explore.p1.note: Figures kept (3,8 triệu, one in three). 'Barriers to education' as 'rào cản trong việc học'; 'displaced inside their own country' paraphrased in plain words; Myanmar kept as the name (check usual Vietnamese form and any political sensitivity).
siteVideo.explore.p1.back: Every learner deserves a chance to explore the world they live in. But across Southeast Asia, many youth face barriers to learning. In Myanmar, about 3.8 million people have had to leave where they live but are still inside their own country. In Malaysia, refugee children cannot go to public schools. And in East Asia and the Pacific, one in every three school-age children has no internet at home.

siteVideo.explore.p2.source: Where schools are stretched, lessons often stick to the basics: reading, maths, and skills for a job. Those matter. But there's little room left for the skills that open up the world: thinking critically, communicating with evidence, and taking other perspectives.
siteVideo.explore.p2.note: 'Stretched' as 'quá tải'; 'skills for a job' as 'kỹ năng để làm việc'. Check naturalness. | Review: "bằng bằng" was awkward; English "communicating with evidence". [Reviewer changed: Ở những nơi trường học đang quá tải, bài học thường chỉ xoay quanh những điều cơ bản: đọc, toán và kỹ năng để làm việc. Những điều đó rất quan trọng. Nhưng còn rất ít chỗ cho những kỹ năng mở ra cả thế giới: suy nghĩ phản biện, trình bày bằng bằng chứng và nhìn từ góc nhìn của người khác. → Ở những nơi trường học đang quá tải, bài học thường chỉ xoay quanh những điều cơ bản: đọc, toán và kỹ năng để làm việc. Những điều đó rất quan trọng. Nhưng còn rất ít chỗ cho những kỹ năng mở ra cả thế giới: suy nghĩ phản biện, trình bày có bằng chứng và nhìn từ góc nhìn của người khác.]
siteVideo.explore.p2.back: In places where schools are overcrowded, lessons often revolve only around the basics: reading, math and skills for work. Those things matter a lot. But there is very little room for the skills that open up the whole world: critical thinking, presenting with evidence, and looking from other people's point of view.

siteVideo.explore.p3.source: Research backs this up. In a Stanford study, students who learned history by questioning real sources grew more in historical thinking, reading, and knowledge than students in regular classes.
siteVideo.explore.p3.note: Stanford kept without 'Đại học'. 'Học sinh' used for the study's students.
siteVideo.explore.p3.back: Research supports this. In a Stanford study, students who learned history by questioning real sources progressed more in historical thinking, reading skills and knowledge than students in ordinary classes.

siteVideo.explore.p4.source: That's why we built Thinkerwell: free lessons in social studies and beyond, for youth facing barriers to education. Our first course, Exploring Our World, has 24 lessons in history, geography, culture, and civic life, and every lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. Every reading has a simpler version and can be read aloud, and lessons work offline, in several languages.
siteVideo.explore.p4.note: Motto 'Social studies and beyond' = 'Khoa học xã hội và hơn thế nữa' (used in p4, p6, session.p6, setup.p6); a native should confirm the motto. 'chúng mình' for the team speaking to learners. 'Nghe đọc thành tiếng' for read aloud. Bahasa Indonesia kept in English form; the video says lessons are in English and Bahasa Indonesia, left as is. | Review: Says lessons work offline "in English and Bahasa Indonesia" (true of the video). In Vietnamese the lessons are also translated; a human should decide whether to add Tiếng Việt to the video script or keep the faithful translation. Changed 11 October 2026: the last words now say lessons work offline 'in several languages' (was 'in English and Bahasa Indonesia'), so the line stays true as languages are added; that part is an AI draft too.
siteVideo.explore.p4.back: That is why we made Thinkerwell: free lessons in social science and more, for youth who face barriers to learning. Our first course, Exploring Our World, has 24 lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life, and each lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. Every reading has an easier version and can be listened to read aloud, and the lessons work without a network, in several languages.

siteVideo.explore.p5.source: Thinkerwell doesn't replace teachers. It lightens their load, with a ready-made guide for every lesson, plus answer keys and printables.
siteVideo.explore.p5.back: Thinkerwell does not replace teachers. The platform makes teachers' load lighter, with ready-made guides for each lesson, plus answers and materials to print.

They write. They talk it through with a partner. They watch a short video, or read it instead. And they reflect.

They read, in standard English or easier English. They write. They talk with a study partner. They watch a short video, or read the written version instead. And they reflect.

siteVideo.session.p5.source: Afterwards, see where every learner is up to. There are no scores, just lessons finished. No devices that day? Every lesson and teacher guide prints in black and white.

pilotDay.intro.source: One page for the adults running a session. Print it and keep it with the devices.

pilotDay.sheetFor.source: For the adults running a session

pilotDay.beforeSetup.source: Set up each device once: open {educators}, then {setup}. The checklist shows what is done on that device.

pilotDay.beforeCodes.source: Print the code cards from {educators}. Each learner types their code as their name.

pilotDay.beforeConsent.source: Check that the permissions agreed with your organisation are in place. If a learner says no, that is the answer, even if the family said yes.

pilotDay.beforeChoose.source: Choose the courses and lessons to teach ({educators}, then {guides}).

pilotDay.startWho.source: Open Thinkerwell on each device. The home page asks {who} Each learner taps their own tile.

pilotDay.startNew.source: New learners tap {new} and type their name or code.

pilotDay.startLook.source: {look} is for visitors. Nothing is saved while someone looks around, so learners should not use it for their own work.

pilotDay.learnStages.source: Most lessons have five stages: {stages}. A lesson with no video has four, without {watch}. Answering the {reflect} question finishes the lesson.

pilotDay.learnStagesNoWatch.source: Every lesson has four stages: {stages}. Answering the {reflect} question finishes the lesson.

pilotDay.learnOrder.source: Nothing is locked. Learners can open any lesson and any stage, in any order, and try the quick checks again.

pilotDay.learnTime.source: A lesson takes about {min}–{max} minutes. Each teacher guide has a plan for {full} minutes and a shorter one for {short}.

pilotDay.wrongDownload.source: Connect to the internet and tap {retry}. Saved work stays on the device.

pilotDay.wrongOffline.source: Keep going. Work saves on the device, and only videos need the internet. Courses other than Exploring Our World need saving in Settings first.

pilotDay.wrongShared.source: Each learner taps their own tile on the home page. Each learner's work is kept apart.

pilotDay.wrongLost.source: Work is saved on the device only, never online. If you saved a file, open {settings}, tap {load} and choose it. Look in the device's downloads for a name that starts with {file}.

pilotDay.wrongVideo.source: Tap {readInstead}. It has the same ideas and works without the internet.

pilotDay.wrongSound.source: This is normal. {listen} and {sayIt} show only where the device can do them. Learners can read and type instead.

pilotDay.topicsNever.source: Never ask learners about their journey, home country, family, religion or ethnicity. Thinkerwell never asks them either.

pilotDay.topicsGuide.source: Before you teach a lesson, read its teacher guide. It starts with {sensitive}, and it says which videos to preview.

pilotDay.topicsGuideNoWatch.source: Before you teach a lesson, read its teacher guide. It starts with {sensitive}.

pilotDay.topicsReview.source: In Exploring Our World, Lessons {first} and {second} ask for a local educator to review them first.

pilotDay.topicsShare.source: If a learner shares something personal, thank them and move on. If you are worried, follow your organisation's safeguarding steps.

pilotDay.endSave.source: Before you reset a device or give it back, save the work to a file: open {settings}, then {transfer}, then {save}. Load the file on the next device.

pilotDay.endCertificates.source: Print certificates for finished sections: open {educators}, then {certificates}.

pilotDay.endClass.source: See where everyone is: open {educators}, then {class}. It shows no scores.

pilotDay.endReview.source: For a course with no section check, ask aloud: the big question, one piece of evidence, what they still want to find out. Then fill in the session record ({educators}, then {feedback}).

feedbackSheet.checkReview.source: For a course with no section check, did you use the three review questions from the session guide?

feedbackSheet.ease.ask.source: Was Thinkerwell easy to use? Think about setting up, finding lessons and starting a session.

feedbackSheet.ease.more.source: What was hard, or what would help?

feedbackSheet.switch.ask.source: Was it clear how to move between courses?

feedbackSheet.content.ask.source: Were the lessons right for your learners?

feedbackSheet.content.more.source: Which lessons were too hard, too easy, or needed care? Write the course and the lesson number.

feedbackSheet.practical.ask.source: What got in the way? Devices, the internet, time, sound, the room, or anything else.

feedbackSheet.anything.ask.source: Is there anything else we should know?

feedbackSheet.privacy.source: Don't write learners' names, or anything they wrote or said. Keep this sheet, or send your answers to Thinkerwell through the contact form.

privacy.intro.source: Thinkerwell provides free social studies learning for youth across Southeast Asia. We are committed to respecting learners’ privacy, dignity and safety. This policy covers our website, communications and learning activities. Its safeguarding commitments apply to everyone under 18 and to anyone working on Thinkerwell’s behalf.

privacy.learnersBody.source: Use a nickname, avoid sharing sensitive personal information, and remember that others using your device may see your saved work. You can skip uncomfortable questions and ask a trusted adult for help.

privacy.s1.p1.source: Learner profiles, preferences, progress and journal responses are saved in the browser on the device used. Shared-device profiles should not be treated as password-protected accounts. Avoid entering addresses, contact details, identity documents or sensitive family information into learning activities.

privacy.s1.p2.source: If you contact us, we receive the information you choose to provide, such as your email address and message. Website hosting and external services may also process technical information, including IP addresses and browser details. Thinkerwell uses information only for the purposes described in this policy.

privacy.s2.p1.source: We limit personal information to what is necessary to provide learning, operate and secure Thinkerwell, respond to enquiries and address safety concerns. We do not sell learners’ personal information or distribute it for advertising or unrelated purposes. Limited sharing is restricted to the service, safeguarding and legal purposes described here. We do not use personal information for targeted advertising or identifiable learner work to train third-party, non-local AI models.

privacy.s2.stats.source: We will collect anonymised, aggregated numerical statistics about platform usage and engagement, such as total visits, lesson activity and feature usage. These statistics help us understand Thinkerwell’s reach and improve the learning experience. They will exclude names, contact details and journal content, and will not identify individual learners. We will not attempt to re-identify anyone from this information.

privacy.s2.statsNow.source: Thinkerwell does not collect these statistics yet. Nothing on the site counts visits, lessons or features today.

privacy.s2.coded.source: An optional feature for pilot partners could link usage data to learner codes. It is switched off for everyone, and nothing is collected through it. Coded data is not anonymous, so it is separate from the statistics above. Any pilot data collection is agreed with each organisation first, with the permissions it needs.

privacy.s2.p3.source: Where consent is required, we explain the purpose clearly and obtain appropriate consent, including from a parent or legal guardian for children under 13 and whenever otherwise required.

privacy.s3.p1.source: Audio, embedded videos and external links may involve other providers, whose privacy practices also apply. We identify relevant providers, cookies or analytics and explain what information they receive. Providers handling information on our behalf must receive only what they need, with appropriate safeguards, including for overseas processing.

privacy.s3.whoIntro.source: These are the only services that receive information from using Thinkerwell. Thinkerwell does not set cookies, and has no ads or analytics from other companies.

privacy.s3.retention.source: Thinkerwell’s own server keeps nothing from the contact form. Copies held by the email services are kept only as long as needed to answer, then deleted. Hosting records are kept by the hosting provider as its policy describes.

privacy.s3.deviceTitle.source: Handled on the device, not sent to a service

privacy.s3.device1.source: Saved work. Profiles, preferences, progress, journal responses and the latest speaking recording stay in the browser’s storage on the device (IndexedDB, with a few small settings in local storage). Nothing is uploaded.

privacy.s3.device2.source: Listen. It reads lessons aloud with recordings delivered with the site, or with a voice already on the device. No lesson text or learner writing is sent to a voice service.

privacy.s3.device3.source: Record yourself. The microphone is used only when a learner taps Start. The clip stays on the device and is never uploaded.

privacy.s3.device4.source: Fonts, pictures and audio. They come from Thinkerwell’s own servers.

privacy.s3.device5.source: AI. No AI service receives learner information. The pretend tool in the Digital World course gives pre-written answers.

privacy.services.vercel.purpose.source: Delivers the website and its files.

privacy.services.vercel.gets.source: Like any web server, it sees the IP address, browser and device details, and the pages requested.

privacy.services.vercel.where.source: Vercel runs servers in several countries, so this may be processed outside the country you are in.

privacy.services.resend.purpose.source: Sends messages from the contact form to our team.

privacy.services.resend.gets.source: What you type in the form: the topic, your name, your email address or WhatsApp number, and your message.

privacy.services.resend.where.source: Resend may process it outside the country you are in.

privacy.services.google.purpose.source: Holds the team’s inbox, so we can read and answer you.

privacy.services.google.gets.source: Every email you send us, and the messages from the contact form.

privacy.services.google.where.source: Google processes information in many countries.

privacy.services.youtube.purpose.source: Plays a lesson video, only after a learner taps play. Every video has a written version.

privacy.services.youtube.gets.source: The player comes from youtube-nocookie.com. Once a video plays, YouTube receives the IP address and browser details, and may use cookies or similar storage on the device.

privacy.services.youtube.where.source: Google processes information in many countries.

privacy.services.speech.name.source: Your browser’s speech service (only if turned on)

privacy.services.speech.purpose.source: Turns speech into text for the Say it button.

privacy.services.speech.gets.source: Off unless an educator turns on “Allow online speech-to-text” in Settings. When it is on, what a learner says is sent to the browser maker’s service.

privacy.services.speech.where.source: This depends on the browser. Read its maker’s privacy policy.

privacy.s4.p1.source: We restrict access to information we hold and use reasonable security measures. We retain it only as long as needed for its stated purpose or legal obligations, then delete or anonymise it. If a data breach occurs, we assess it and notify affected people and authorities where required.

privacy.s4.p2.source: Contact us to request access, correction, deletion or withdrawal of consent. We will explain any applicable limits. Clearing Thinkerwell’s browser data can remove all locally saved profiles and work on that browser. We cannot remotely retrieve or erase information held only on your device. Others with access to that browser may still be able to see it.

privacy.s4.remove.source: On the “Who’s learning today?” screen, Remove deletes one learner’s lesson work, journal, section check scores and recordings from that device. It cannot be undone.

privacy.s5.p1.source: We prohibit abuse, exploitation, harassment, bullying and discrimination. Team members must follow safeguarding conduct rules and receive preparation and suitability checks appropriate to their roles. Direct learner sessions must have responsible adult supervision; secret contact and unsupervised private sessions are prohibited.

privacy.s5.p2.source: We review materials for age suitability. Learners and organisations may skip sensitive activities or use fictional examples without sharing personal experiences. Partners and Thinkerwell must agree on supervision, consent and local reporting arrangements before joint activities.

privacy.s6.p1.source: We do not routinely record learner sessions. Using identifiable images, recordings, quotations or work requires specific parent or guardian permission and the child’s agreement. Refusing does not affect learning access. Permission never justifies material that could put a child at risk.

privacy.s7.p1.source: Contact {email} for privacy requests, unsuitable content or safeguarding concerns. Share only necessary details. Reports will be taken seriously, handled without retaliation and shared only with people who need to respond. Absolute secrecy cannot be promised where protection or legal reporting requires disclosure. Concerns involving team members must receive independent handling.

privacy.s7.p2.source: Journals are not monitored for safety concerns, and our inbox is not an emergency service. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services or a safe, trusted adult.

privacy.s7.p3.source: We review this policy annually and after significant changes or incidents, and publish its latest revision date.
